title: 덕분에 재밌었다고 전해줘요  (Tell Him I Had Fun Thanks to Him)

segments.t: Back at the quiet KBS variety office instead of attending his own welcome party, Baek Seung-chan gets a kind word from senior producer Ryu Il-yong before the desk phone rings. On the line is Youn Yuh-jung, calling about a jar of homemade plum tea she left on Ra Joon-mo's desk. Listen for "maesilcha", 'plum tea', and "nongdam", 'a joke'.
나 윤여정인데요. 거기 라준모 피디 자리죠?
내가 라 피디 주려고 담근 매실차예요.
Let's walk through this late-night office call turn by turn.
'Anyway, I welcome you.' Before heading home to his kids, Il-yong cheers Seung-chan up with "eojjaetdeun", 'in any case', and warm plain-style "hwanyeonghanda", 'I welcome you'.
'Hello?' Alone among empty desks, Seung-chan picks up the ringing receiver with "yeoboseyo".
나 윤여정인데요. 거기 라준모 피디 자리죠?

'This is Youn Yuh-jung. That is Producer Ra Joon-mo's desk, right?' Koreans introduce themselves on the phone with "na ...-indeyo", 'it's me, so-and-so', and "jari" means someone's 'seat' or 'office desk'.
'Yes, that is right.' Standing straight even on the phone, Seung-chan replies "ne, matseumnida" — crisp, formal confirmation for 'that's correct'.
내가 라 피디 주려고 담근 매실차예요.
'It is plum tea I steeped to give Producer Ra.' "Damgeun" describes homemade preserves or syrups steeped by hand, and "maesilcha" is sweet green-plum tea, a beloved Korean digestive drink.
'Please tell him I had fun thanks to him.' All her anger gone, Yuh-jung chooses "deokbune", 'thanks to your efforts', paired with "jaemisseotdago jeonaejwoyo", 'please pass along that I enjoyed it'.
'Yes, I will be sure to pass that along.' Seung-chan adds "kkok", 'without fail', before humble "jeonaedeurigesseumnida", promising to deliver her message respectfully.
'By the way, who is answering the phone?' Shifting topics with "geunde", Yuh-jung uses "bun", the polite word for 'person', inside "nugusinga", 'who might you be?'.
'I'm going to sue you. Just kidding.' Recognizing the rookie from her van, she teases him with "gosohada", 'to file a lawsuit', before immediately smiling it off with "nongdamiya", 'it's a joke!'.
'What is your name?' Dropping to warm elder speech, she asks "neo ireumi mwoya", pairing "ireum", 'name', with "mwoya", 'what is it?'.
'I am Baek Seung-chan.' To introduce yourself formally in any Korean workplace, attach "-imnida" straight onto your full name.

'All right, Producer Baek Seung-chan. Good work today.' Calling him a full producer by title for the very first time, she signs off with "sugohaesseoyo, oneul" — 'you worked hard today'. Now let's hear the whole phone call again from start to finish.
나 윤여정인데요. 거기 라준모 피디 자리죠?
내가 라 피디 주려고 담근 매실차예요.
From "matseumnida" for crisp confirmation to "nongdamiya" for a friendly tease and "sugohaesseoyo" at the end of a long shift, those lines carry real warmth. Until next time!
